message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference list of **Canadian federal holidays** that created “long weekends” during 2023.  
(“Observed” means the legal day off when the actual holiday fell on a weekend.)

| # | Federal Holiday | Calendar Date | Observed (if applicable) | Why It Made a Long Weekend |
|---|-----------------|---------------|--------------------------|----------------------------|
| 1 | New Year’s Day   | Sun Jan 01 | Mon Jan 02               | Off on Monday after the weekend |
| 2 | Family Day       | Mon Feb 20 | —                        | Already a Monday → 3‑day stretch |
| 3 | Good Friday      | Fri Apr 07 | —                        | Friday + Sat/Sun = 3‑day weekend |
| 4 | Victoria Day     | Mon May 22 | —                        | Monday → 3‑day weekend |
| 5 | Canada Day       | Sat Jul 01 | Mon Jul 03                | Observed Monday after the weekend |
| 6 | Labour Day       | Mon Sep 04 | —                        | Monday → 3‑day weekend |
| 7 | Thanksgiving    | Mon Oct 09 | —                        | Monday → 3‑day weekend |
| 8 | Christmas Day    | Mon Dec 25 | —                        | Monday → 3‑day weekend |
| 9 | Boxing Day       | Tue Dec 26 | —                        | Tuesday + Wed/Thu = 3‑day stretch |

> **Note:** Some provinces observe *additional* holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, Civic Holiday in British Columbia, etc.) which could extend other weekends. The above table covers the nationwide federal holidays that guaranteed a long weekend anywhere in Canada during 2023.
